Counsel for Applicant :- Pandey Balkrishna,Prashant Kumar Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard Mr. Yatindra, learned counsel, assisted by Mr. Ajay Singh Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Vishwajeet, who is involved in Case Crime No. 1514 of 2022, under Sections 354, 354-Ka, 376, 384, 506, 120B IPC and Section 5-L/6, 7/8 POCSO Act and Section 67A Information Technology Act, police station Sahibabad,
district Ghaziabad, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

As per prosecution case, in brief, informant, who is father of the victim, lodged the first information report on 18.09.2022 against the applicant with the allegation inter alia that the applicant used to visit his house.

In the year 2019, when his daughter was the student of XIIth standard, one day finding her alone, the applicant made physical relation with her in his house and also took her obscene photographs and made video and thereafter, on the pretext of the said photographs and Vishwajeet vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139146136/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is neighbour of the informant and is working as Accountant in the HDFC Bank.
He has been falsely implicated in this case for ulterior purpose.
There is no photographs of the victim with the applicant and nothing has been recovered from the possession of the applicant.
Referring the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. of the victim, it is also pointed out that the victim did not disclose even the date of the incident.
The applicant does not have any criminal history to his credit.
Lastly, it is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 20.09.2022 and in case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant but does not dispute the above factual aspect of the matter as argued on behalf of the applicant.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that in the first information report, no specific date and time of the incident is mentioned and even assuming that incident took place in the year 2019, even then the F.I.R. has been lodged after about 3 years.

It is admitted that on the date of alleged incident, the victim was student of XIIth standard,
therefore, she was capable to under the things which has happened to her.
Even then, no complaint was made by her within reasonable period of time, therefore, the applicant has made out a case for bail.
Hence, the bail application of the applicant is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant Vishwajeet, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned.
In case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail.
